statement: A symmetric, unimodal shape (Gaussian-like or flat-top) will yield a higher R than the constant function because it makes the autoconvolution flatter in the center.
refuted_if: Gradient ascent from such shapes fails to exceed 2/3 by a margin.

statement: The main limitation of p0002 is its O(N) finite-difference gradient: an exact/adjoint gradient makes each iteration O(N log N), so many more iterations and much larger N become affordable, which should raise R well above 0.810.
refuted_if: An exact-gradient L-BFGS refinement at N=200, then upsampled to N>=1000, fails to improve p0002 by at least 0.005.

statement: R is maximized by shapes whose mass is concentrated near one edge, making the autoconvolution peak near the boundary and sparse; p0005 is an example, and even more extreme left-edge concentration may yield higher R.
refuted_if: Multi-start from strongly left-concentrated seeds and high-resolution refinement of p0005 fail to exceed 0.833241 by a meaningful margin.

statement: Exact analytic gradients plus L-BFGS-B make high-N refinement cheap, but gains depend on re-optimizing after each upsampling step and preserving the sparse/asymmetric structure.

Exact analytic gradients plus L-BFGS-B make refinement cheap, but measured gains come mainly from repeated perturb-and-reoptimize at fixed N=400; raw upsampling to N>=800 without new perturbations did not help.

The p0006 basin is a strong local optimum at N=400; more aggressive structural perturbations at N=400, or applying the exact-gradient perturbation method to the alternate p0008 basin, may yield further gains, while raw upsampling and more extreme edge concentration do not.
refuted_if: Aggressive basin-hopping at N=400 and exact-gradient refinement of p0008 both fail to exceed 0.8522.

statement: The p0011 extreme-edge basin is under-resolved at N=400; exact-gradient refinement at N=800/1600 with reoptimization after each upsample and sparsity-preserving perturbations will raise R above 0.8565.
refuted_if: Multi-resolution exact-gradient refinement of p0011 fails to exceed 0.8565.

statement: Exact analytic gradients plus L-BFGS-B make refinement cheap, and measured gains come mainly from repeated perturb-and-reoptimize. Raw upsampling without reoptimization has not helped, but the p0011 extreme-edge basin may benefit from higher N when each upsample is reoptimized.
The p0006 basin is a strong local optimum at N=400, but it is not the best basin: the extreme-edge p0008/p0011 line, when refined with exact gradients and perturbations, is substantially better.

Exact-gradient L-BFGS-B is a cheap, reliable refiner; most gains come from perturb-and-reoptimize. Raw upsampling without reoptimization does not help, and the old p0011 basin is already resolved at N=400. The new p0012 boundary-spike basin is far more extreme, so test whether it is under-resolved at N=400 via N=800/1600 with reoptimization.

The p0012 construction is not the bottom of its extreme boundary-concentrated basin: richer support-relocating structural moves followed by exact-gradient L-BFGS can push the autocorrelation peak closer to the boundary and/or sparsify the support further, raising R above 0.8684.
refuted_if: Three units of expanded structural perturbations from p0012 fail to exceed 0.8684 by at least 0.0003.

statement: Exact-gradient L-BFGS-B plus repeated perturb-and-reoptimize at fixed N=400 is the cheap reliable refiner; raw upsample ladders contribute nothing even on the narrow p0012/p0014 basin (p0014's 400->800->1600 stages were flat). The gain attributed to upsampling in F12 actually came from perturbation at N=400. Gains now depend on structural relocation of the narrow spike support, and repeated conti…

The p0014 extreme-boundary spike arrangement is not exhausted: richer structural relocations (left-compress, spike move/split, block scale/zero, mirror, threshold) followed by exact-gradient L-BFGS-B can push R above 0.8735, because p0012->p0014 and p0012->p0016 show the basin responds to support relocation.
refuted_if: Three units of corrected rich structural perturbation from p0014 fail to exceed 0.8735 by at least 0.0003.

statement: The p0014 shape is sparse enough that its effective spikes may be narrower than one N=400 step; representing each nonzero block as a half-width sub-block at N=800 (doubling height, zeroing the neighbor) before exact-gradient reoptimization can improve R, whereas plain interpolation upsampling cannot.
refuted_if: The split-spike N=800/1600 test fails to exceed 0.8735 by at least 0.0003 while N=400 perturb continues to improve.

statement: p0018's narrow spikes may still be under-resolved at N=400: replacing each nonzero block by a half-width, doubled-height sub-block on an N=800/1600 grid, then exact-gradient reoptimization, can raise R above 0.87357. p0017 was inconclusive, so this remains untested rather than refuted.

The 0.8736 basin is a local optimum of the extreme-edge single-spike family; a sparse multi-spike comb seed (several separated narrow spikes optimized jointly) can reach a qualitatively different basin and exceed 0.8736, because a comb makes f*f flatter than a single boundary-concentrated spike.
refuted_if: Two units of multi-spike comb seeds on N=400/800, refined by exact-gradient L-BFGS-B and perturb-and-reoptimize, fail to exceed 0.87357 by at least 0.0003.

statement: The earlier flat multi-resolution ladders were an interpolation artifact: linear upsampling of a narrow spike changes the step function before reoptimization. Exact zero-order-hold upsampling (each N=400 cell replaced by identical sub-cells) preserves the step function and lets exact-gradient L-BFGS-B refine sub-cell structure, potentially raising R above 0.87357.
refuted_if: Step-preserving upsampling to N=800/1600 with exact-gradient and perturb reoptimization fails to exceed 0.87357 by at least 0.0003.

statement: Exact-gradient L-BFGS-B plus perturb-and-reoptimize is the reliable local refiner at fixed N, but linear-interpolation upsample ladders contribute essentially nothing. Step-preserving upsampling is untested and may behave differently.

Exact-gradient L-BFGS-B plus perturb-and-reoptimize is the reliable local refiner at fixed N, but neither linear nor exact zero-order-hold upsampling ladders add real gains: the plateau is structural, not a grid-resolution artifact.

The 0.87358 plateau is a strong structural attractor for greedy L-BFGS perturb loops; escaping it requires non-local search that accepts worse states or a different parameterization of the sparse support.
refuted_if: A funded non-local search (annealing or continuous spike parameterization) from p0023 fails to exceed 0.87358 by at least 0.0003.

statement: The extreme-edge sparse spike shape is not the global optimum; a different structural family or a non-greedy support rearrangement can exceed 0.8740.
refuted_if: Multiple funded non-local searches and fresh structural families all return below 0.8739.
